name: Spicy Pork Patties

instructions.detail: Put the ground pork (1 lb), egg (1), breadcrumbs (¼ cup), onion powder (2 tsp), garlic powder (2 tsp), paprika (1 tsp), chili powder (1 tsp), cumin (½ tsp), oregano (½ tsp), cayenne pepper (1 tsp), and red pepper flakes (1 tsp) in a bowl. Mix thoroughly.
Form into 8-9 balls and flatten into a patty shape, approximately 10-15% larger than your bread.
Put a large pan on medium-high heat.
Add the patties and cook to an internal temp of 160°F, flipping halfway. About 7 minutes per side.

description: Homemade breakfast sausage patties from ground pork, egg and breadcrumbs, seasoned hot with cayenne, chili powder and red pepper flakes.

name: Scrambled Eggs

instructions.detail: Crack 2 eggs into a bowl, add 1 Tbsp milk and 1 tsp Tony's seasoning. Whisk until combined.
Pour into a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Gently fold the eggs with a spatula until just set.

description: Soft scrambled eggs made with 2% milk and a shake of Tony's seasoning.

name: Oatmeal

ingredients.text: Jelly or fresh fruit, for serving (optional)

instructions.detail: Add the milk (7 cups), water (1 cup), oats (2 cups), maple syrup or honey (2 Tbsp) and salt (2 tsp) to a slow cooker.
Cook on low for 8 hours. Stir every 2 hours if possible.
When 2 hours remain, stir, then add the frozen fruit (3 cups).
Serve with jelly or fresh fruit for added sweetness.

description: Steel-cut oats cooked in milk and water, sweetened with maple syrup or honey and topped with frozen fruit.

name: Pulled Pork

ingredients.text: 3-4 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-3 large pieces
2 tsp seasoned salt (1 tsp if the pork was dry-brined)

instructions.detail: Pat the pork (3-4 lb) dry and coat all over with the seasoned salt (2 tsp) and pepper (½ tsp).

Heat the oil (1 Tbsp) in a large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Brown the pork hard on every side, 7-10 min total. This is the only browning the dish gets - nothing browns inside a slow cooker.

Spread the onion (1, sliced) over the bottom of the slow cooker. Whisk the barbecue sauce (½ cup), mustard (1 Tbsp), vinegar (1 Tbsp), brown sugar (1 Tbsp), soy sauce (1½ tsp), onion powder (1 Tbsp) and garlic powder (1 Tbsp). Pour the water (2 Tbsp) into the hot skillet, scrape up the fond and whisk it into the sauce. Set the pork on the onions and pour the sauce over.
Lid on. High for 1 hour, then Low for about 6-7 hours. Done at 195-205°F, when it pulls apart with no resistance. Don't lift the lid before then.
Lift the pork out to rest. Skim the fat off the juices. Reduce the juices by about half: lid off on High for 30-45 min, or faster in a wide skillet at a hard simmer, about 10 min.
Shred the pork and discard the fatty seams. Toss with the reduced juices, then add barbecue sauce (about ½ cup) until slightly wet.

description: Seared boneless pork shoulder slow cooked in a tangy mustard, vinegar and barbecue sauce, then shredded into its own reduced juices.

name: Pepperoncini Beef
source: Adam's build, Mississippi pot roast lineage; technique corrected against the slow cooker reference

ingredients.text: 1 jar (16 oz) whole pepperoncini, ¼ cup of the brine reserved separately
¼ cup reserved pepperoncini brine (3 Tbsp before the reduction, 1 Tbsp off the heat)

instructions.detail: The night before, pat the chuck roast (3½ lb) dry and season every surface with the table salt (2½ tsp) - about 1% of the roast's weight. Set on a rack over a sheet pan and refrigerate uncovered 8 to 24 hours. Uncovered is the point: it dries the surface for the sear. Use 1%, not the 1.25 to 1.5% an oven braise wants, because a jar of brine, soy sauce (2 Tbsp), and Worcestershire (3 Tbsp) are all going in and nothing will evaporate to give you room later.

Blot the roast (3½ lb) bone dry. Heat the neutral oil (2 Tbsp) in a heavy skillet over medium-high until it shimmers and the first thread of smoke appears. Sear 3 to 4 minutes per face until genuinely dark brown, not tan - 7 to 10 minutes total. Transfer to the slow cooker. Not optional: nothing inside a slow cooker ever reaches the roughly 300F browning threshold, so unlike an oven braise there is no second chance from surfaces above the liquid line.

Pour off all but about 1 Tbsp of fat. Drop to medium, add the sliced onion (1 large) and cook 6 to 8 minutes until translucent with browned edges. Add the smashed garlic (6 cloves) for the last 30 seconds. Add the tomato paste (2 Tbsp) and stir constantly 60 to 90 seconds, until it darkens from bright red to brick and smells nutty instead of tinny. Deglaze with the brine from the pepperoncini jar, scraping the pan floor with a flat wooden spatula until the fond releases and the floor goes bare.

Scrape the whole pan - onions, fond, brine - over the roast. Add the pepperoncini from the jar, the Worcestershire (3 Tbsp), the soy sauce (2 Tbsp), and the chiles de arbol (4 whole). Add no stock, no broth, and no water. It will look like far too little liquid. It is not: the roast releases 1 to 2 cups of its own and a sealed cooker evaporates almost none of it, so the pot finishes with more liquid than it started with. Adding stock here is the single most common way to ruin this dish. Lid on, Low for 9 to 10 hours, first hour on High if you can. Root vegetables, if you use them, go quartered on the bottom and against the sides before the meat - the element is a wire belt around the lower side wall, not a disc underneath, and roots cook slower than the beef.

At 9 hours, push a thin metal skewer or paring knife tip into the thickest part. It should slide in and, more importantly, slide back out with zero grip - like pushing into cold butter. Any resistance means another 45 to 60 minutes. Internal lands at 195 to 205F, but temperature only tells you when to start testing. Do not stretch it to 12 hours: past the window the collagen holding the fiber bundles together has dissolved and the roast goes shredded and stringy at the same time.

Lift the beef out and hold it under foil. Let the liquid settle 10 minutes and skim the fat off with a ladle - there will be a lot, and a slow cooker never boils it back into the sauce the way a hard simmer would. Stir in 3 Tbsp of the reserved brine, then reduce with the lid off, cooker on High, 30 to 45 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon. Do not salt before this step - whatever is in there concentrates now.

Off the heat, stir in the last 1 Tbsp of reserved brine and taste for salt for the first time. That final off-heat acid is what keeps ten hours of braise from reading heavy and flat, and it only works if it has not been boiled. Shred or slice the beef, return it to the sauce to warm through without boiling, and serve with the pepperoncini. For more heat than the peppers give, ground cayenne or hot sauce goes in during the last hour of the cook, never at the start - both turn bitter over a long hold.

description: Chuck roast slow cooked with a whole jar of pepperoncini and its brine, onion, garlic and tomato paste until it shreds.

name: Beef Stew

ingredients.text: 5 russet potatoes, washed, cut into large cubes

instructions.detail: Pat the chuck roast (2.5 lb) dry, coat both sides with salt and pepper, and sear in a hot pan on the stove about 2 minutes per side.

Add the carrots (5), onion (1, quartered), celery (5 stalks), and potatoes (5) to the slow cooker. Nestle the seared beef on top, then add the onion soup mix (2 packets) and steak sauce (1 cup). Cook on low 8 hours.
At the 7-hour mark, lift out the beef and stir the vegetables. Let the beef cool, then cut into cubes.
Return the cubed beef to the cooker, stir everything together, and finish the last hour.

description: Slow cooker beef stew with chuck, potatoes, carrots, celery and onion, seasoned with onion soup mix and steak sauce.

name: Pork Stew

ingredients.text: 5 russet potatoes, washed, cut into large cubes
1 can (12 oz) frozen apple juice concentrate

instructions.detail: Coat the pork tenderloin (2.5 lb) on both sides with salt and pepper and sear about 2 minutes per side on the stove.

Add the carrots (5), onion (1, quartered), celery (5 stalks), and potatoes (5) to the slow cooker. Set the tenderloin on top, then add the onion soup mix (1 packet) and frozen apple juice concentrate (1 can). Cook on low 5 hours.
About 1 hour before the end (around the 4-hour mark), lift out the tenderloin and stir the vegetables. Let the pork rest at least 5 minutes, then slice into medallions.
Return the medallions to the stew and serve.

description: Slow cooker pork tenderloin stew with potatoes, carrots, celery and onion, sweetened with apple juice concentrate.

name: Corned Beef and Cabbage

ingredients.text: 3 lb corned beef brisket (with seasoning packet)
1 can (12 oz) frozen apple juice concentrate
5 russet potatoes, washed, cut into large cubes

instructions.detail: Remove the seasoning packet from the corned beef and tie it into a tea strainer so the spices flavor the liquid but stay contained.

Add the corned beef (3 lb), carrots (5), onion (1, quartered), and potatoes (5) to the slow cooker with the frozen apple juice concentrate (1 can) and the strained seasoning packet. Cook on low 8-10 hours.
Add the cabbage wedges (1 head) for the last 1-2 hours so they soften without turning to mush.
Discard the seasoning packet, slice the corned beef against the grain, and serve with the vegetables.

description: Corned beef brisket slow cooked in apple juice with potatoes, carrots, onion and cabbage wedges.

name: Rib Rub

instructions.detail: Combine the brown sugar (½ cup), paprika (2 Tbsp), garlic powder (1 Tbsp), onion powder (1 Tbsp), seasoned salt (1 Tbsp), chili powder (1 tsp), black pepper (1 tsp), white pepper (½ tsp), nutmeg (½ tsp), and coriander (½ tsp) in a bowl and whisk until the brown sugar is broken up and the blend is uniform in color.
Pat the ribs dry, then coat all sides generously with the rub, pressing it in. For best results, wrap and rest in the fridge 1-12 hours before cooking.
Keep leftover rub in an airtight container away from heat and light. Makes about ¾ cup; keeps for several months.

description: A sweet, smoky dry rub for ribs: brown sugar and paprika with garlic, onion, chili powder, two peppers, nutmeg and coriander.

name: Noodle Dough

ingredients.text: 3 cups all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled, plus more for dusting
Semolina or extra all-purpose flour, for dusting the cut sheets
2 Tbsp table salt, for the blanching water

instructions.detail: Makes about 1¼ lb dough, enough for 12 to 14 lasagna sheets or 4 servings of cut noodles. Mound the all-purpose flour (3 cups) on a board or in a wide bowl and make a well in the center. Add the eggs (4), the egg yolk (1), the olive oil (1 Tbsp), and the salt (1 tsp). Break the yolks with a fork and pull flour in from the walls of the well until you have a shaggy, uneven mass with no dry pockets left. Add the water (1 to 2 Tbsp) only if flour refuses to take up. Do not knead yet.

Cover with an inverted bowl and leave it 30 minutes. This is a modified autolyse: enzymes naturally present in the flour begin breaking weak protein bonds while the flour hydrates fully, which makes the dough measurably more extensible and cuts the kneading needed to reach the same gluten development. It is the highest-leverage step in the recipe if you are rolling by hand.

Knead 6 to 8 minutes, pushing with the heel of your hand, folding, and giving the dough a quarter turn each time. Stop when it is smooth and slightly tacky. Do not chase a windowpane. Overworking builds the elastic snap-back that fights a rolling pin.

Wrap tightly in plastic and rest at room temperature at least 1 hour. This is stress relaxation in the gluten network, and skipping it means the sheet retracts every time you lift the pin. The dough holds overnight in the refrigerator; bring it back to room temperature before rolling.

Cut the dough into 4 pieces and keep three covered. On a lightly floured surface, flatten one piece and roll from the center outward, rotating the sheet a quarter turn every two or three passes so it thins evenly rather than going long and narrow. If it starts pushing back, set it down, cover it, and give it 10 minutes before continuing.

Roll to about 1/16 inch for lasagna, thinner for cut noodles. To gauge it without a machine dial, lay the sheet over a printed page: you should be able to read the text through it, but the letters should look soft-edged rather than sharp. Sharp text means too thin for lasagna and the sheet will dissolve into the sauce. Fully opaque means too thick and the layers will read as bready.

For lasagna, cut each sheet into rectangles roughly 4½ inches wide by 9 inches long, which lays three across a 9x13 pan. For noodles, flour the sheet well, roll it loosely, and slice to the width you want. Dust the cut pieces on both faces with semolina, which is coarse enough that it does not hydrate and turn to glue, and stack them on a towel-lined sheet pan with parchment between layers.

Bring 4 quarts of water to a rolling boil and salt it at 1 percent by weight: 2 Tbsp table salt. Work in batches of 3 or 4 sheets for 45 to 60 seconds each, then lift straight into a bowl of cold water to stop the cooking. Lay flat on damp towels in a single layer, barely oiled, until you are ready to build. Cut noodles for serving need 90 seconds to 2 minutes and no shock.

Use all-purpose flour (3 cups) rather than a high-gluten or semolina-heavy blend: protein content drives elastic recoil, and the 10 to 12 percent range of all-purpose is what makes a hand-rolled sheet cooperate. Brand matters within that range, so add the full water (2 Tbsp) if your flour runs high in protein. The olive oil (1 Tbsp) and the extra yolk (1) both work by coating flour particles and interfering with gluten formation, buying extensibility and tenderness at a dose small enough to keep the structure the sheet needs to survive the blanch. Blanching is worth the step because it rinses off surface starch that otherwise sets into a gluey seam between layers, and it pre-gelatinizes the sheet so the bake is about melting and setting rather than cooking raw pasta.

description: Fresh egg noodle dough from all-purpose flour, whole eggs, an extra yolk and olive oil, rolled thin for cutting into noodles.

name: Wheat Bread Dough

ingredients.text: ⅓ cup whole milk, warmed to ~110°F
2¼ tsp active dry or instant yeast (1 standard packet)
1 tsp fresh lemon juice (or apple cider vinegar)
1⅓ cups whole wheat flour (plus more as needed)

instructions.detail: Whisk warm water (1 cup), warm milk (⅓ cup), and yeast (2¼ tsp) in a large bowl. Add 2 cups flour and stir until a thick batter forms. Cover and let double in size at room temperature, about 60-90 minutes.

Add honey (3 Tbsp), butter (3 Tbsp), lemon juice (1 tsp), remaining flour (1⅓ cups), and salt (1¼ tsp). Using a dough hook or by hand, mix on medium until dough pulls away from sides, about 3 minutes.
Knead in mixer or by hand on a lightly floured surface for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Lightly grease a large bowl. Place dough in bowl, turning to coat. Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 1.5-2 hours until doubled.
Grease a 9×5-inch loaf pan.
Punch down dough to release air. On a lightly floured surface, roll into an 8×15-inch rectangle. Roll up into an 8-inch log and place in loaf pan.
Cover shaped loaf and let rise until about 1 inch above the top of the pan, about 45-60 minutes.
Adjust oven rack to a lower position and preheat to 350°F.
Optional: Brush risen loaf with beaten egg white, then sprinkle oats (1 Tbsp) on top.
Bake for 36-40 minutes until golden brown. Bread is done when it sounds hollow when tapped, or an instant-read thermometer reads 195-200°F.
Remove from oven and cool for a few minutes in pan on a cooling rack before slicing.

description: A honey whole wheat sandwich loaf enriched with milk and butter, baked in a 9x5 pan with an optional oat topping.

name: Garlic Butter Chicken and Potatoes Skillet

ingredients.text: ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce (or coconut aminos)
1½ lb chicken breast, cut into strips
Crushed red pepper flakes, to taste (optional)
Salt and fresh cracked pepper, to taste

instructions.detail: Toss the chicken strips (1½ lb) with soy sauce (¼ cup), olive oil (2 Tbsp), hot sauce (2 Tbsp) and a pinch of pepper. Set aside while you do the potatoes.
Boil the quartered potatoes (1½ lb) in salted water for 8 minutes. Drain.
Heat olive oil (1 Tbsp) and butter (1 Tbsp) in a large skillet over medium-high. Sauté the potatoes 4 minutes, stir, then 4-5 minutes more until golden and fork-tender. Move to a plate.

Drop to medium and add the remaining butter (2 Tbsp). Lift the chicken from the marinade (keep the marinade) and lay it in the skillet with the garlic (5 cloves) and chili flakes if using. Cook 1 minute per side until lightly browned.
Pour in the reserved marinade and simmer a few minutes, until it thickens and the chicken reaches 165°F. Stir in dried sage (1 tsp), onion powder (1 tsp) and garlic powder (1 tsp).

Return the potatoes with thyme (1 tsp), rosemary (1 tsp) and oregano (1 tsp); toss and heat through 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Off the heat, fold in the spinach (1 cup), scatter the Parmesan (½ cup) over and serve.

description: Chicken breast and baby potatoes seared in one skillet and finished in garlic butter with fresh herbs and spinach.

name: Meatloaf

instructions.detail: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Combine ground beef (2 lb), ground pork (1 lb), onion soup mix (2 packets), eggs (2), panko (1 cup), and Worcestershire sauce (2 Tbsp). Mix until just combined.
Mix ketchup (½ cup), brown sugar (¼ cup), lemon juice (1 Tbsp), and mustard (2 tsp) in a small bowl.
Shape meat mixture into a loaf in a baking pan. Spread half the glaze on top.
Bake for 1 hour. Apply remaining glaze during the last 15 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 160°F.
Let rest 10 minutes before slicing.

description: Beef and pork meatloaf seasoned with onion soup mix and Worcestershire, baked under a sweet ketchup and brown sugar glaze.

name: Marinated Chicken Drumsticks

instructions.detail: Combine the honey (2 Tbsp), soy sauce (2 Tbsp), Worcestershire sauce (2 Tbsp), lime juice (1 Tbsp), hoisin sauce (1 Tbsp), olive oil (¼ cup), garlic (5 cloves, minced), onion powder (1 Tbsp), garlic powder (1 Tbsp), and salt and pepper. Add chicken drumsticks (2 lb) and marinate for 4-8 hours.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Set a wire rack over a baking pan.
Place drumsticks on wire rack. Cook for 30-35 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Broil for 3-5 minutes until skin is crispy.

description: Chicken drumsticks marinated in honey, soy, Worcestershire, hoisin and lime, then roasted on a rack and broiled crisp.

name: Soy-Garlic-Paprika Drumsticks

ingredients.text: 1½ tsp table salt (for the dry brine)
4 cloves garlic, grated on a microplane
2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (or 1 Tbsp gochugaru)

instructions.detail: Pat the drumsticks (8, about 2½ lb) completely dry. Rub table salt (1½ tsp) over all sides. Set on a wire rack over a sheet pan and refrigerate uncovered 5 to 6 hours. Uncovered is load-bearing - airflow dries the skin while the salt migrates inward. This step, not the marinade, is what makes the skin crisp.

About 1 hour before cooking, warm olive oil (3 Tbsp) to roughly 325 F. Off the heat, stir in grated garlic (4 cloves), smoked paprika (1 Tbsp), crushed red pepper flakes (2 tsp), dried oregano (1 tsp), and coarse black pepper (1 tsp). Cool to room temperature. Capsaicin and the paprika carotenoids are both fat-soluble and barely dissolve in cold oil; thirty seconds in hot fat releases multiples more of both.

Into the cooled oil, stir soy sauce (2 Tbsp), brown sugar (1 Tbsp), and lemon juice (1 Tbsp). Soy is cut from ¼ cup because the dry brine already salted the meat - at full volume with the brine this comes out aggressively salty.
Rub the paste over the drumsticks 60 minutes before cooking, no earlier. The paste is a surface coat; left on for hours it only re-wets the skin the dry brine spent all afternoon drying out.
Wipe off standing liquid with paper towels; leave the clinging garlic and paprika. Surface water must boil off before the skin can brown, and the sugar will not caramelize through a wet film.

Heat oven to 425 F. Space the drumsticks on a wire rack set over a sheet pan. Roast 35 to 40 minutes, turning once at the halfway point. The rack keeps them out of their own rendered fat, which would steam the undersides gray.

Pull at 170 to 175 F at the thickest point, probe angled away from the bone. Rest 5 minutes. Dark meat should run past the 165 F safety line - collagen breaks down in the higher band and texture improves rather than drying out.

Skin side up over indirect heat until the thickest part reads 170 F, then blot the paste off and finish skin-side down over the coals 2 to 3 minutes. Blotting is not optional here - sugary, oily surface coatings are the standard flare-up ignition source, and sustained flame turns the skin acrid.

The sweet-soy glaze wants something plain and crisp across from it - a roasted potato side and a sharp green vegetable both work. Roast a side on a lower rack while these are on the upper one; anything that runs at 425 F shares the oven without adjustment.

description: Dry-brined chicken drumsticks seasoned with soy sauce, grated garlic, smoked paprika and oregano.

name: Seared Chicken Breast with Cranberry-Thyme Pan Sauce

ingredients.text: 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 6 oz each)
1 tsp fresh thyme (or ½ tsp dried)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Small splash of vinegar or lemon juice

instructions.detail: Simmer the chicken stock (⅔ cup) with the dried cranberries (¼ cup), sliced onion (¼ small), Dijon (1 tsp), maple syrup (1 tsp), thyme (½ tsp), and a pinch of salt and pepper for 2-3 minutes. Pull off heat, cover, and let sit several hours so the cranberries rehydrate. Hold the butter and acid until service - they break down if added now.

Butterfly each chicken breast (2, about 6 oz each) to an even thickness. Season both sides with table salt (½ tsp), black pepper (½ tsp), fresh thyme (1 tsp), and rubbed sage (½ tsp). Let it sit while the pan heats - even 15 minutes of dry-brining seasons deeper than surface salt does.

Pat the breasts dry - dry meat is what gives you a real sear. Heat the oil (1 Tbsp) in a skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Cook 4-5 minutes per side until deep golden, pulling the chicken at an internal temperature of about 157F. Rest 5 minutes. Chicken breast is pasteurized by time at temperature, not by hitting 165F instantly - held near 157F it reaches the same safety in under a minute, and it stays juicy. Past 165F in the pan is where breast turns to sawdust.

Reheat the cranberry base and simmer 2 minutes to a light nappe, loosening with a splash of stock if it thickened while soaking. Off heat, swirl in the cold butter (1 Tbsp) and a small splash of vinegar or lemon juice. Spoon over the rested chicken.
Steam or blanch the green beans (12 oz) 3-4 minutes, then toss in butter (1 Tbsp) with a smashed garlic clove (1) and salt to taste. Top with toasted sliced almonds (2 Tbsp) if you want.
Serve with mashed potatoes or stuffing and the green beans or another green vegetable such as brussels sprouts.

description: Pan-seared chicken breast with a quick pan sauce of chicken stock, onion, dried cranberries, thyme and sage.

name: Skillet Beef and Potato Hash with Fried Eggs

ingredients.text: 2 lb russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
Reserved rendered beef fat (about ¼ cup, drained from the beef)
Salt, black pepper, and paprika, for the eggs
Steak sauce, ketchup, or barbecue sauce, for serving

instructions.detail: Peel the potatoes (2 lb) and cut into ½-inch dice. Boil in well-salted water for 20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance. Drain and let them sit in the colander 2-3 minutes to steam-dry. A wet potato surface is pinned at 212F and cannot brown, so this pause is doing real work.

In a bowl, mix the ground beef (1 lb, 80/20) with paprika (1½ tsp), garlic powder (1 tsp), onion powder (1 tsp), chili powder (½ tsp), ground cumin (½ tsp), salt (1 tsp), and black pepper (½ tsp). Season before it hits the pan, not after - the spices are fat-soluble and bloom in the fat as it renders.

Cook the seasoned beef (1 lb) in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high, breaking it up. As fat and juice pool, tip it off into a heatproof cup and reserve. Drain a second time once more renders. 80/20 gives up more fat than the pan can use, and beef sitting in liquid is held at 212F and will not brown. Do not discard the fat - it is the cooking medium for everything that follows.

instructions.step: Fry the Beef in Its Own Fat
instructions.detail: Return a spoonful of the reserved beef fat to the pan. Press the beef flat and leave it alone 3-4 minutes, then flip; repeat 2-3 times, adding reserved fat a spoonful at a time whenever the surface goes dry and dull. You are frying it now, not steaming it. Move it to a plate.

Add about 2 Tbsp of the reserved beef fat and the sliced onion (1 large). Cook 8-10 minutes over medium-high until the edges are deep brown. Sliced, not minced - it holds its texture through the rest of the cook.

Add the drained potatoes (2 lb) with paprika (1 Tbsp), garlic powder (1 tsp), onion powder (1 tsp), salt (1 tsp), and black pepper (½ tsp). Toss to coat and cook 2-3 minutes to soften and take on the fat.

Return the beef to the pan. Press the whole thing flat, leave it 4 minutes without stirring, flip in sections, and go another 4 minutes. Two or three passes total. Add reserved beef fat a spoonful at a time any time the pan looks dry - dry means the crust stops forming.
Turn the heat to low, scatter the shredded cheddar (½ cup) evenly over the top, cover for 1 minute, and pull it off the heat.

In a separate pan, fry the eggs (4 large) in a spoonful of the reserved beef fat, seasoned with salt, black pepper, and paprika. Yolk sets at about 158F and white does not fully set until about 185F, so cover the pan for 1-2 minutes to set the whites by steam and pull while the yolks are still loose. Cooking the eggs directly on top of the hash works but the hash keeps feeding them heat and they overshoot.
Slide the eggs onto the hash and serve immediately with steak sauce, ketchup, or barbecue sauce. This is not a garnish - the hash reads dry without one.

description: Spiced ground beef and diced potatoes cooked in one skillet and topped with fried eggs.

name: Sheet-Pan Paprika Chicken Thighs with Potatoes

ingredients.text: 1½ lb baby Yukon Gold potatoes, halved

instructions.detail: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle position.
In a small bowl, stir together the smoked paprika (1 Tbsp), garlic powder (2 tsp), dried oregano (1 tsp), cayenne (½ to 1 tsp), table salt (1½ tsp), and black pepper (1 tsp).
On a rimmed sheet pan, toss the halved potatoes (1½ lb) with olive oil (2 Tbsp) and about a third of the seasoning mix. Spread them cut-side down. Roast 20 minutes by themselves.
instructions.why: Boneless thighs cook in roughly half the time bone-in do, so the potatoes need the head start.

instructions.detail: While the potatoes roast, pat the chicken thighs (2 lb) dry with paper towels, then toss them in a bowl with the remaining olive oil (2 Tbsp) and the rest of the seasoning mix.
Pull the pan out, push the potatoes to the edges, and lay the thighs (2 lb) in the middle, smooth side up and not touching. Roast another 18-20 minutes, until the thighs read 175°F.
instructions.why: Do not crowd the pan - touching thighs steam instead of roast.

instructions.detail: Broil 2-3 minutes at the end.
instructions.why: Boneless skinless thighs have no skin or bone fat to self-baste, so they come out pale and flat without this step.

instructions.detail: Rest 5 minutes on the pan, then squeeze the lemon (1, cut into wedges) over everything.
instructions.why: Resting on the pan lets the potatoes pick up the rendered fat.

description: Boneless chicken thighs and baby Yukon Golds roasted on one sheet pan with smoked paprika, garlic, oregano and cayenne.

name: King Ranch Chicken Casserole

ingredients.text: 1 can (10 oz) diced tomatoes with green chiles (Rotel), undrained
12 corn tortillas, torn into large pieces

instructions.detail: Strip the meat off the rotisserie chicken (1 whole) in large shreds, about 4 cups. Discard skin and bones. Large shreds hold texture through the bake; chopped fine, the chicken disappears into the sauce.

Melt the butter (4 Tbsp) in a saucepan over medium. Whisk in the flour (¼ cup) and cook 2 to 3 minutes, whisking, until it smells nutty and turns the color of wet sand. Stop there. A darker roux tastes better on its own but thickens roughly half as well, which is the wrong trade in a casserole that has to hold its sauce.

Whisk the chicken broth (3 cups) in a little at a time, keeping it smooth. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon. Cook it slightly thicker than looks right, because it loosens in the oven.

Off the heat, stir in the diced tomatoes with green chiles (10 oz, undrained), diced green chiles (4 oz), chili powder (2 tsp), ground cumin (1 tsp), garlic powder (1 tsp), chipotle powder (1½ tsp), table salt (1 tsp) and black pepper (½ tsp). Cool 2 minutes, then stir in the sour cream (½ cup) off the heat so it does not break.

Spread a thin film of sauce across the bottom of a 9x13 pan. Lay down a third of the torn corn tortillas (12 total), then half the chicken (about 2 cups), half the sliced onion (1 medium), a third of the sauce, and 1 cup of the shredded sharp cheddar (3 cups total).

Repeat: a third of the corn tortillas (12 total), the remaining chicken (about 2 cups), the remaining sliced onion (1 medium), a third of the sauce, and 1 cup of the shredded sharp cheddar (3 cups total).
Finish with the last third of the corn tortillas (12 total) and the last third of the sauce. Hold the final 1 cup of shredded sharp cheddar (3 cups total) back for the end of the bake.
Cover the pan tight with foil. Bag the remaining shredded sharp cheddar (1 cup) separately. Refrigerate, or travel in a cooler if the dish is being baked somewhere else.
Pull the pan out and leave it on the counter while the oven comes to 375F, about 25 minutes. A pan straight from the refrigerator or a cooler adds 8 to 10 minutes to the bake and heats unevenly.
Bake covered at 375F for 35 minutes.

Uncover, scatter the remaining shredded sharp cheddar (1 cup) over the top, and bake uncovered 12 minutes until melted and browning at the edges. It is done when the center reads 165F and the edges are bubbling, so go by that rather than the clock. Do not hold it in the oven past browning; extra time only thins the sauce.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting so it slices instead of sliding.

description: Tex-Mex chicken casserole in a scratch roux sauce with diced tomatoes, green chiles and sour cream, baked until bubbling.

name: Picadillo

instructions.detail: Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add ground beef (1 lb) and cook, breaking up the meat, until mostly browned. Drain grease and return to heat.
Add diced onion (½ cup), green bell pepper (1), and potatoes (2 cups). Continue cooking over medium heat until onion and peppers are softened. Add garlic (4 cloves) and cook an additional 30 seconds.
Pour in tomato sauce (8-16 oz) and beef broth (½ cup). Add salt (1 tsp), pepper (¼ tsp), cumin (1 tsp), coriander (1 tsp), and bay leaf (1). Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 10 minutes.
Remove lid, stir, and continue cooking uncovered for 10 minutes until potatoes are soft and most liquid is gone.
Serve warm with flour tortillas and rice.

description: Ground beef simmered with potato, green bell pepper, onion and garlic in tomato sauce and beef broth.

name: Taco Pasta

ingredients.text: 4 oz Velveeta, cut into cubes (can sub ¾ cup shredded cheese)
1 can (10 oz) Rotel tomatoes with green chilies, undrained

instructions.detail: Shred cheddar and Monterey Jack from a block. Let cheese come to near room temperature before adding to sauce.
Cook and crumble ground beef (1 lb) in a high-walled pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Drain grease.
Melt butter (1 Tbsp) in the same pot. Add garlic (2 cloves) and cook for 1 minute.
Add taco seasoning (1 packet), Worcestershire sauce (1 Tbsp), tomato paste (2 Tbsp), beef broth (1 cup), chicken broth (1 cup), milk (1 cup), and Rotel tomatoes (1 can). Stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle boil. Add pasta shells (½ lb) and submerge. Cover and cook according to package instructions, stirring halfway through.
Remove cover and ensure pasta is cooked. Taste-test for doneness. Cover and cook longer if needed.
Turn heat to low. Gradually stir in all three cheeses until melted.
Sauce will thicken as it stands. Serve once desired consistency is reached.

description: Taco pasta with seasoned ground beef in a three-cheese sauce of cheddar, Monterey Jack and Velveeta.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Carnitas

instructions.detail: Rinse and dry the pork shoulder (4 lb). Mix olive oil (1 Tbsp), salt (2 tsp), cumin (2 tsp), chili powder (2 tsp), black pepper (1 tsp), oregano (1 Tbsp) and cayenne (¼ tsp); rub all over the pork.
Place the pork fat-cap-up in the slow cooker. Top with the onion (1), jalapeño (1) and garlic (4 cloves); pour over the orange juice (¾ cup).
Cook on low for 10 hours or high for 7 hours, until tender enough to shred.
Rest the pork briefly, then shred with two forks. Skim the fat from the juices. If more than 2 cups remain, reduce to about 2 cups.

Heat olive oil (1 Tbsp) in a large skillet over high heat. Spread the pork and drizzle with juices; let the juices evaporate and the bottom turn golden and crusty. Turn and briefly sear the other side. Work in batches - do not crowd the pan.
Drizzle with the remaining juices just before serving. Serve hot in tacos.

description: Pork shoulder slow cooked with orange, lime, onion, jalapeño, garlic and cumin, then shredded and crisped.

name: Mexican Coleslaw

instructions.detail: Combine the slaw mix (16 oz bag), lime juice (2 limes), olive oil (3 Tbsp), honey (2 Tbsp), dried oregano (1 tsp), mayo (¼ cup), Greek yogurt (¼ cup), and salt and pepper to taste in a large bowl.
Refrigerate for 1+ hours before serving.

description: A light slaw of bagged coleslaw mix in a lime, honey and oregano dressing with mayo and Greek yogurt.

name: Broccoli Chicken Stir Fry

ingredients.text: ¼ cup green onion whites, cut into 1-inch pieces
¼ cup carrot, thin-sliced on diagonal

instructions.detail: Soak the broccoli (16 oz) in clean water 10-15 min, dunking and rinsing. Cut florets from stem, slicing up from the stem with a paring knife to keep buds intact. Peel stem skin and slice thin. Return everything to clean water, rinse again, drain.

Slice chicken breast (12 oz) thin. Combine cornstarch (1 Tbsp), water (2 Tbsp), salt (½ tsp), oyster sauce (1 Tbsp), and white pepper (¼ tsp); mix until cornstarch dissolves, then squeeze the marinade into the chicken with your hand. Set aside.
Smash, peel, and mince the garlic (2 cloves). Peel and cut ginger (1 Tbsp) into small triangles. Slice green onion whites (¼ cup) into 1-inch pieces. Peel carrot (¼ cup) and cut thin on a diagonal.

Sauce: combine oyster sauce (1 Tbsp), light soy sauce (1 Tbsp), salt (½ tsp), sugar (1½ tsp), cooking wine (2 tsp), white pepper (⅓ tsp). Set aside. Slurry: stir cornstarch (1 Tbsp) into water (2 Tbsp). Keep separate until the last step.

Bring water (8 cups) to a rolling boil. Add salt (1 tsp) and oil (2 tsp) - keeps the broccoli bright green. Add broccoli; the moment water returns to a boil, pull it out (4-5 min max). Shock in ice water 1 min, drain, set aside.

Heat wok on high until smoking. Add oil (2 Tbsp), drop heat to low. Lay chicken in a single layer; let it brown undisturbed ~30 sec before flipping. Stir fry until just cooked through, ~2 min total. Remove and set aside.

Add garlic (2 cloves), ginger (1 Tbsp), green onion whites (¼ cup), and carrot (¼ cup) to the hot wok; stir fry 30-40 sec until fragrant. Crank heat to high. Add broccoli and cooking wine (1 tsp); stir fry 1½-2 min. Return chicken; stir fry 30 sec. Pour sauce into the wok center; toss 15-20 sec. Taste - add sugar (½ tsp) if needed. Drizzle in slurry while stirring, ~30 sec, until glossy and lightly coated. Finish with sesame oil (1 tsp), toss once, kill the heat. Plate immediately.

description: Restaurant-style stir fry of velveted chicken and blanched broccoli in a light oyster and soy sauce.

name: Peanut Butter Noodles

ingredients.text: ¼ cup water or chicken broth

instructions.detail: Toss the chicken breasts (2) with cornstarch (1 Tbsp), water (2 Tbsp), salt (½ tsp), oyster sauce (1 Tbsp) and white pepper (¼ tsp). Heat neutral oil (1 Tbsp) in a wok or large skillet and cook the chicken through to 165°F, then slice or shred.

Whisk peanut butter (1 cup), soy sauce (¼ cup), water or chicken broth (¼ cup), rice vinegar (2 Tbsp), toasted sesame oil (1 Tbsp), oyster sauce (2 Tbsp), sriracha (2 Tbsp), honey (2 Tbsp), onion powder (2 tsp), garlic powder (2 tsp), ground ginger (2 tsp), red pepper flakes (½ tsp), white pepper (½ tsp) and black pepper (½ tsp). Set aside.
Cook the brown rice noodles (16 oz) per package directions. Scoop out ¼ cup of the noodle water, then drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking.
Heat oil (1 Tbsp) in the wok over high heat. Add the carrots (2, julienned) and cabbage (1 package) and cook 3-4 minutes.
Add the garlic (3-5 cloves) and green onions (1 bunch) for the last 1-2 minutes.
Add the noodles, chicken and sauce and toss, loosening with the reserved noodle water (up to ¼ cup) as needed.
Heat through and serve immediately.

description: Brown rice noodles with chicken, cabbage and carrots tossed in a peanut butter and soy sauce.

name: Salt and Pepper Chicken

ingredients.text: 1 lb chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions.detail: Combine garlic (3 cloves, minced), salt (1 tsp), brown sugar (2 tsp), water (2 Tbsp), rice wine (1 Tbsp), baking soda (¼ tsp), and soy sauce (2 Tbsp). Stir to dissolve sugar.
Add chicken pieces (1 lb) to marinade and toss to coat. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Beat egg in one bowl. Place cornstarch (¾ cup) in another bowl.
Drain chicken from marinade. Dip each piece in egg wash, then coat thoroughly in cornstarch.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry chicken in batches (do not overcrowd), about 4-5 minutes per batch until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Return fried chicken to pan. Toss with salt (½ tsp) and pepper (½ tsp) to taste. Garnish with chopped green onions (2 Tbsp) and serve hot.

description: Bite-size chicken coated in egg and cornstarch, fried crisp and tossed with garlic, green onion, salt and pepper.

name: Thai Pineapple Fried Rice

ingredients.text: ½ red bell pepper, diced (~¾ cup)
1½ cups pineapple pieces, fresh or canned drained

instructions.detail: Heat vegetable oil (2 Tbsp) in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add garlic (2 cloves) and onion (½). Cook for 1 minute.
Add red bell pepper (½) and cook for 1 minute.
Add frozen peas (½ cup) and stir for 30 seconds.

Add day-old rice (3 cups), oyster sauce (1 Tbsp), fish sauce (1½ Tbsp), sugar (½ tsp), soy sauce (1½ Tbsp), and Thai seasoning (1 Tbsp). Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes until rice is caramelized.
Add pineapple pieces (1½ cups) and stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Stir through green onions (½ cup) and serve immediately.

description: Day-old jasmine rice stir fried with pineapple, peas, bell pepper and onion in oyster, fish and soy sauce.

name: Asian Spinach Salad

ingredients.text: ¼ cup extra virgin olive oil

instructions.detail: Whisk together olive oil (¼ cup), rice vinegar (¼ cup), honey (1½ Tbsp), sesame oil (3 Tbsp), soy sauce (1½ tsp), salt, and garlic.
Toss spinach (3 cups) with cranberries (½ cup) and walnuts (½ cup). Drizzle with dressing and serve.

description: Spinach with dried cranberries and walnuts in a rice vinegar, sesame and soy dressing.

name: Pork Char Siu

instructions.detail: Slice the pork shoulder (2 lb) into 1-inch strips.
Use a fork to poke many holes all over each piece to help the marinade absorb.
In a bowl, combine garlic salt (1 Tbsp), brown sugar (4 Tbsp), oyster sauce (2 Tbsp), soy sauce (2 Tbsp), hoisin sauce (2 Tbsp), red wine vinegar (2 Tbsp), and mirin (1 Tbsp).
Add pork to the marinade and refrigerate for 8-24 hours.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Place pork on a wire rack set over a pan with about ¼ cup water (add more water as needed to prevent burning).
Reserve extra marinade. Roast the pork and baste with the marinade every 15 minutes.
After 45 minutes (on the third baste), switch to a diluted honey glaze and cook for an additional 10 minutes.
Remove from oven and let rest for 10 minutes.
Slice and serve over rice with steamed vegetables and sauce of your choice.

description: Chinese barbecue pork in a sweet glaze of hoisin, oyster sauce, soy, brown sugar and mirin.

name: Sesame Beef and Noodles

instructions.detail: Cook the egg noodles (8 oz) according to package directions. Drain and set aside.

Whisk together the soy sauce (¼ cup), water (¼ cup), rice wine vinegar (3 Tbsp), sesame oil (2 Tbsp), honey (2 Tbsp), Sriracha (2 Tbsp), oyster sauce (2 Tbsp), chili sauce (1 Tbsp), garlic (4 cloves, minced), ground ginger (1 tsp), black pepper (1 tsp), and salt (1 tsp). Set aside.
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef (1 lb) and cook, breaking it up, until browned, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Drain fat. Remove beef and set aside.

Return the pan to medium-high heat. Add the onion (1 medium, sliced) and carrots (3, sliced into strips). Stir fry 3-4 minutes until beginning to soften. Add the frozen broccoli (1 bag, 12 oz) and stir fry another 2-3 minutes.
Return the beef (1 lb, cooked) to the pan. Add the noodles (8 oz, cooked) and pour in the sauce. Toss to combine and cook 2 minutes.
Stir together the cornstarch (1 Tbsp) and water (2 Tbsp) to form a slurry. Add to the pan and stir until the sauce tightens, about 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Add the fresh spinach (3 cups) and let sit 2 minutes off heat to steam and wilt. Toss to incorporate and serve.

description: Ground beef and egg noodles with broccoli, carrots and spinach in a sweet-spicy sesame, soy and Sriracha sauce.

name: Sticky Chinese Pork Belly

ingredients.text: 2.2 lbs rindless pork belly, sliced and halved (each piece about finger-length)
1 thumb-sized piece fresh ginger, peeled and minced
4 thumb-sized pieces fresh ginger, peeled and minced
1 tsp rice vinegar (added to reserved portion only)
2 medium carrots, sliced on the bias

instructions.detail: Add pork belly (2.2 lbs), hot chicken stock (4¼ cups), minced ginger (1 thumb-sized piece), garlic (3 cloves, roughly chopped), rice wine (1 Tbsp), and sugar (1 Tbsp) to a heavy-based pot or cast iron casserole. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer for 2 hours.
Remove pork from the braising liquid and pat thoroughly dry with paper towels. Reserve the liquid if desired - excellent base for an Asian noodle soup. Cut pork into bite-sized chunks.

Whisk together minced ginger (4 thumb-sized pieces), red chilies (4, finely chopped), honey (½ cup), brown sugar (½ cup), dark soy sauce (¾ cup), garlic powder (1 Tbsp), and onion powder (1 Tbsp) in a bowl. Divide into 4 equal portions. Transfer 1 portion to a small bowl, stir in rice vinegar (1 tsp), and set aside. The remaining 3 portions go into the pan.

Heat half the vegetable oil (¼ cup) in a wok or large skillet over medium-high. Add onion (1 medium, sliced) and carrots (2 medium, sliced on the bias); cook stirring until softened, about 4 minutes. Add broccoli florets (1 head) and cook until bright green and just tender-crisp, about 3-4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a large bowl and set aside.

Heat remaining vegetable oil (¼ cup) in the same pan over medium-high. Add pork chunks (2.2 lbs) with a pinch of salt and pepper. Fry, turning regularly, until golden and beginning to crisp on the edges, about 5-7 minutes. Use a splatter guard - rendered pork fat will pop aggressively at this stage.

Add diced red bell pepper (1) and cook until softened to your preference, about 2-3 minutes. Pour ¾ of the total glaze (3 portions) over the pork and pepper. Cook, turning the pork frequently, until dark and sticky, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the cooked vegetables back in and fold into the pork mixture until evenly coated. For large batches, add in two additions so the pan stays hot.

Pour the reserved glaze portion with rice vinegar (1 tsp) over everything and fold to combine. If the sauce needs thickening, sprinkle in xanthan gum (start with ¼ tsp) and toss until the sauce tightens to your liking.
Serve over cooked white rice topped with chopped spring onions and chopped red chilies.

description: Pork belly braised in chicken stock with ginger, garlic and rice wine, then cooked down to a sticky glaze.

name: Keema Aloo Bhuna with Peas, Carrot and Spinach

ingredients.text: 1 lb russet potatoes (about 2 medium), peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
1 large yellow onion, halved and sliced thin
2 medium carrots, cut into ¼-inch dice (about 1 cup)
5 oz fresh spinach, stacked and cut into ¼-inch ribbons
Plain whole-milk yogurt, for the table

instructions.detail: Put the diced potatoes (1 lb, cut into ½-inch dice) in cold salted water, bring to a boil, and cook 7 to 8 minutes - a knife should meet slight resistance at the center. Drain and leave them in the colander to steam dry while everything else happens. Dry surfaces are what let them take a fried face later; ½-inch dice turns to mush well before the 20 minutes a whole potato wants.

Mix the ground beef (1 lb, 80/20) by hand with the salt (1¼ tsp), cumin (2 tsp), coriander (2 tsp), turmeric (1 tsp), cayenne (¾ tsp) and black pepper (½ tsp) until the color is even. Season before the pan, not after.

Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high until a drop of water skates. Add the beef (1 lb), press it flat into one slab, and leave it 3 to 4 minutes. Flip in large pieces, press again, 3 minutes. Pour the rendered fat into a bowl. Repeat the press-and-flip once or twice more, draining a second time, until the beef is in browned crumbles with real crust - about 10 minutes total. Move the beef to a plate. Reserve the drained fat and discard about 2 Tbsp of it.

Return 2 Tbsp of the reserved beef fat to the pan over medium heat. Add the sliced onion (1 large) and a pinch of salt; cook 7 to 8 minutes, scraping the fond up as the onion releases its water, until soft and golden at the edges. Beef fat rather than neutral oil is the point - spice flavor is fat-soluble, so the fat that carries it should already taste like the dish.

Add the garlic (5 cloves, minced), ginger (1 Tbsp, grated) and serrano (1, sliced thin). Stir constantly for 45 seconds, no longer. The onion is buffering the pan heat; minced garlic on bare hot metal burns in about that same 45 seconds and there is no recovery from it.
Add the tomato paste (2 Tbsp) and fry it, stirring, 1 to 2 minutes, until it darkens from red to brick and fat separates at the edges. That split is the signal the raw-paste flavor is gone.

Add the carrots (1 cup, cut into ¼-inch dice) and the water (½ cup). Simmer uncovered, stirring now and then, 5 to 6 minutes, until the water is gone and the pan is sizzling in fat again. No lid - a lid steams the pan and costs the dry style.

Return the beef and add the par-boiled potatoes (1 lb) plus another 1 to 2 Tbsp of the reserved beef fat. Stir in the garam masala (1½ tsp). Press the mixture flat and leave it 2 to 3 minutes, then turn it in sections and press again - twice more, about 8 minutes total. Browned faces on the potato, not a stir. This step is the dish.
Scatter the frozen peas (1 cup) over the top and fold through; 2 minutes, just to heat.
Add the spinach ribbons (5 oz) in two handfuls, folding until collapsed - 60 to 90 seconds. Kill the heat.

Squeeze in the lime juice (1 Tbsp) and scatter the cilantro (¼ cup). Lime goes in off heat and after the spinach for two reasons: citric acid is volatile and dies with sustained heat, and acid turns chlorophyll to pheophytin, so lime added before the greens gives you olive-drab leaves. Taste for salt. Serve with plain whole-milk yogurt at the table.

description: Dry-style ground beef and potato curry with peas, carrot and spinach, fried in its own fat and finished with lime.

name: Honey-Garlic Soy Glazed Chicken Tenderloins

instructions.detail: Pull the tendons from the chicken (1 lb): pin the end of the white tendon with a paper towel and slide a fork down it. Pat the pieces very dry. Toss with the cornstarch (2 Tbsp) and black pepper (¼ tsp) to a thin, even coat. In a small bowl, whisk the soy sauce (2½ Tbsp), honey (3 Tbsp), cooking sherry (2 Tbsp), water (2 Tbsp), rice vinegar (1 tsp) and red pepper flakes (½ tsp). The soy is trimmed from the usual 3 to 4 Tbsp because cooking sherry is already salted.

Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, add the neutral oil (1½ Tbsp) and wait for it to shimmer. Lay the chicken in a single layer with space between pieces. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, until golden and it releases from the pan. Flip and cook 2 minutes more. It does not need to be cooked through yet. Move it to a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium. Add the garlic (4 cloves, minced) to the oil left in the pan and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.

Stir the glaze mixture and pour it in. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until it turns syrupy. The cornstarch that came off the chicken is what thickens it, so no slurry is needed. Return the chicken and any juices and toss 1 to 2 minutes, until glossy and the thickest piece reads 165°F. Keep the heat at medium: honey scorches fast. If the glaze gets too thick before the chicken is done, add a splash of water.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the toasted sesame oil (1 tsp) and scatter the green onions (2, sliced) over the top. Serve over rice.

description: Cornstarch-dusted chicken tenderloins seared hard, then tossed in a quick honey, garlic and soy glaze in the same skillet. Serve over rice.

name: Spicy Peanut Chicken

ingredients.text: 1½ lb boneless skinless chicken breast (about 2 large), cut into 1-inch pieces
⅓ cup natural peanut butter, stirred well first

instructions.detail: Start the rice first; everything else fits inside its cook time. Pat the chicken (1½ lb, cut into 1-inch pieces) dry and toss it with the soy sauce (1 Tbsp) and cornstarch (1 Tbsp). Let it sit while you make the sauce. The cornstarch gives the sauce something to grip and helps keep the peanut-oil-and-water sauce from separating.

In a bowl, whisk the peanut butter (⅓ cup), soy sauce (2 Tbsp), lime juice (2 Tbsp), honey (1 Tbsp), garlic (3 cloves, grated) and chili crisp (2 Tbsp). Whisk in the hot water (⅓ cup) a splash at a time. It looks broken and stiff at first, then turns smooth and pourable. The soy is the salt here, so there is no separate salt; if your chili crisp is a salty brand, cut the soy in the sauce to 1½ Tbsp.

Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until the neutral oil (1 Tbsp) shimmers. Add half the chicken in a single layer and leave it alone for 2 minutes to brown, then toss and cook 2 minutes more, until the biggest piece reads 165°F. Move it to a plate. Repeat with the remaining neutral oil (1 Tbsp) and chicken. Two batches matter: a full load drops the pan below browning temperature and the chicken poaches gray in its own juice.

Turn the burner down to low and return all the chicken to the pan. Pour in the sauce and toss 30 to 60 seconds, until glossy and coating every piece. Keep it on low: peanut butter scorches fast and tightens on heat. If the sauce gets too thick, loosen it with hot water, 1 Tbsp at a time.
Spoon over the rice and top with the roasted peanuts (¼ cup, chopped) and green onions (2, sliced), if using.

description: Bite-size chicken breast seared hard in two batches, then tossed on low in a quick natural peanut butter, soy, lime, honey, garlic and chili crisp sauce. Serve over rice.

name: Lasagna

ingredients.text: ½ lb hot Italian sausage, casings removed
2 Tbsp olive oil, only if the reserved beef fat runs short
1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
12 to 14 fresh egg pasta sheets, about 4½ by 9 inches, blanched (see Noodle Dough), or 12 no-boil dried sheets
1 lb low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella, shredded from a block

instructions.detail: Set the whole-milk ricotta (15 oz) in a fine-mesh sieve over a bowl and leave it 30 minutes while you build the sauce. Whole-milk ricotta carries enough free water to turn the bottom of the pan to soup, and there is no fixing it after the bake.

In a bowl, work the dried oregano (1½ tsp), crushed fennel seed (1 tsp), crushed red pepper (1½ tsp), black pepper (1 tsp), and salt (1 tsp) into the ground beef (1½ lb) with your hands. Leave the Italian sausage (½ lb) unseasoned; it is already salted and spiced, and stacking salt on salt is how this gets away from you.

Heat a wide heavy skillet over medium-high. Add the seasoned ground beef (1½ lb) and press it flat into one even slab. Leave it undisturbed 3 to 4 minutes, flip, and repeat, flipping two or three times total. Drain the rendered fat into a heatproof cup partway through and again near the end, reserving all of it. Add the fat back a spoonful at a time as the pan goes dry so the beef fries rather than steams. Transfer the beef to a bowl.

Add the Italian sausage (½ lb) to the same pan, break it into rough chunks, and brown hard for 5 to 6 minutes. Transfer it to the bowl with the beef. Leave the browned fond on the pan floor; it is concentrated Maillard product and it carries the sauce's bass notes.

Pour about 3 Tbsp of the reserved beef fat back into the pan, topping up with olive oil (2 Tbsp) if you are short. Drop the heat to medium, add the onion (1½ cups), carrot (¾ cup), and celery (¾ cup), and cook 8 to 10 minutes until the onion is translucent and the edges take color. Add the garlic (6 cloves) for the final 30 seconds.

Add the tomato paste (3 Tbsp) and stir constantly for 60 to 90 seconds, until it darkens from bright red to brick and smells nutty instead of tinny. Under-blooming it leaves a raw metallic note that survives the entire simmer.

Add the dry red wine (1 cup) and scrape the pan floor with a flat wooden spatula while it boils, pushing rather than stirring, until the floor goes bare. Let the wine reduce by half, 4 to 5 minutes. Do not shortcut this: wine added and never reduced leaves a sharp boozy edge that 90 minutes of simmering will not remove.

Return the beef and sausage with any collected juices. Add the hand-crushed whole tomatoes (28 oz can), crushed tomatoes (15 oz can), whole milk (½ cup), Parmigiano-Reggiano rind (1 piece), and bay leaves (2). Bring it to a full simmer, meaning steady streams of small bubbles breaking the surface roughly one to three per second rather than a boil, then drop to a bare simmer and cook uncovered 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes. It should reduce to a thick sauce that mounds on a spoon. If it is still loose at 90 minutes, raise the heat and keep going, because a wet sauce is the leading cause of a lasagna that will not slice.

Pull the Parmigiano rind (1 piece) and bay leaves (2). Off heat, stir in the red wine vinegar (2 tsp). The tomato and wine were cooked-in acid building depth; this late addition is for brightness, and it is what keeps a long-simmered meat sauce from tasting heavy and flat. Taste and correct the salt now, after the reduction, never before it.

Combine the drained ricotta (15 oz), egg (1), grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (¾ cup), parsley (⅓ cup), black pepper (½ tsp), nutmeg (¼ tsp), and salt (½ tsp). The egg is doing structural work: its proteins coagulate in the oven and hold the filling as a distinct layer instead of letting it slump into the sauce.

Heat the oven to 375F. Spread about 1 cup of the meat sauce across the bottom of a 9x13 pan. Lay 3 blanched pasta sheets crosswise with the edges just overlapping. Spread a third of the ricotta filling, scatter a quarter of the shredded mozzarella (1 lb total), then about 1½ cups of meat sauce. Repeat that sequence twice more. Finish with a fourth layer of sheets, the remaining meat sauce, the remaining mozzarella, and the grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (¾ cup).

Tent foil over the pan so it does not touch the cheese and bake 40 minutes. Remove the foil and bake another 20 to 25 minutes, until the top is browned in patches and the edges are bubbling. The uncovering is the entire browning step: under foil the surface is parked at 212F by trapped steam, and nothing browns at 212F. If it is still pale at 25 minutes, run the broiler 2 to 3 minutes and watch it continuously.

Rest 30 minutes out of the oven before cutting. This is not optional. Cut into it hot and you get a plate of slurry, because the starch and egg matrix has to cool and set before it will hold a slice. Scatter the torn basil (¼ cup) at service.

Shred the mozzarella (1 lb) from a block rather than buying it pre-shredded, which is dusted with cellulose to stop clumping and melts grainy. Mozzarella is a long-protein, high-melt cheese that stretches; Parmigiano-Reggiano is the opposite, high in protein and low in moisture, and it breaks if melted into a sauce, which is why it goes into the filling and onto the top as a dry crust instead. The sauce is better on day two, since soluble flavor compounds keep diffusing at refrigerator temperature long after the cook, so make the sauce a day ahead if you want to split the work. Cool it in containers no deeper than 2 inches, uncovered in an ice bath for 20 minutes, then refrigerate uncovered before lidding; do not put a hot covered pot straight into the refrigerator.

description: Beef and hot Italian sausage lasagna with a whole-milk ricotta layer, built in one 9x13 pan.

name: Persian Chicken

instructions.detail: Soak the basmati rice (1½ cups) in a big bowl of water for at least 30 minutes.

Mix salt (1 tsp), cinnamon (1½ tsp), cumin (1 tsp), coriander (1 tsp), black pepper (1 tsp), cardamom (½ tsp), allspice (½ tsp), nutmeg (¼ tsp) and cloves (¼ tsp). This makes about 7 tsp; you will use it in thirds of about 2⅓ tsp.
Coat the chicken thighs (6) with one third of the spice blend (about 2⅓ tsp).

Heat olive oil (3 Tbsp) in a large pan. Add the garlic (4 cloves) and red onion (1), season with the second third of the spice blend (about 2⅓ tsp) and sauté until soft and browned. Set aside for the garnish.
In the same pan, cook the chicken about 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 175°F. Set aside.
Add the water (2 cups) to the pan and bring to a boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it with the turmeric (¼ tsp) and the last third of the spice blend (about 2⅓ tsp).
Cover and simmer on low for 15-20 minutes, until the rice is cooked.
Set the chicken on top of the rice. Garnish with the sautéed onions and garlic and the almonds (¼ cup).

description: Bone-in chicken with turmeric, onion and garlic, served over basmati rice and garnished with almonds.

name: Lebanese Potato Salad

ingredients.text: ¼ cup spring onions, finely chopped
1 Tbsp dried mint, finely chopped (fresh is also good)
¼ cup extra virgin olive oil

instructions.detail: Place the washed potatoes (1⅔ lb) in a large pot, cover with cold water by about 2 inches. Bring to a gentle boil over high heat, then reduce to medium. Cook until fork-tender - do not overcook.
Let potatoes cool slightly. Cut into even bite-sized chunks (with or without skin).
In a large bowl, add potato chunks, spring onions (¼ cup), parsley (¼ cup), mint (1 Tbsp), and optional garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil (¼ cup), lemon juice (¼ cup), salt, and black pepper.
Pour dressing over potato mixture and gently toss to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve warm or chilled.

description: Mayo-free potato salad dressed with olive oil and lemon, with parsley, spring onion and dried mint.

name: Lebanese Kafta (Ground Beef Skewers)

instructions.detail: Finely chop the onion (1 medium), parsley (1 cup) and mint (1 Tbsp), by hand or by pulsing in a food processor. Stop before it turns to paste.
Crush the garlic (3 cloves) into a paste.

In a large bowl, combine the ground beef (2 lb) with the chopped onion, parsley and mint, the garlic paste, table salt (1½ tsp), black pepper (2 tsp), cayenne (1 tsp), and allspice, cinnamon, cloves, coriander, cumin and nutmeg (½ tsp each). Mix well, then cover and refrigerate for 1-24 hours.
Form the meat onto skewers, no more than 1 inch in diameter.
Grill over medium heat until the internal temperature reaches 160°F.

description: Lebanese ground beef skewers with onion, parsley, mint, allspice and cinnamon, grilled to 160°F.

name: Lebanese Cucumber Salad

instructions.detail: Add the cucumber (1 large, finely diced), yogurt (1 cup), ground mint (½ tsp, heaping), garlic (1 clove, crushed), and salt (½ tsp) to a mixing bowl and combine.
Adjust salt if needed. Serve cold.

description: Cool yogurt and cucumber salad with garlic and dried mint.

name: Wasabi Egg Salad

ingredients.text: ¾ tsp wasabi paste (start at ½ tsp, up to 1 tsp)

instructions.detail: Bring 1 inch of water to a rolling boil in a wide pot. Set the eggs (12 large) straight from the fridge into a steamer basket in a single layer, cover, drop to medium heat, and steam 13 minutes. Cold eggs into hot steam is what makes them peel.
Move the eggs (12 large) to an ice bath of 4 cups ice and 4 cups cold water for 15 minutes. Crack all over and peel. Shells should slip.
Halve each of the eggs (12 large) lengthwise. Lay each half flat side down and cut lengthwise into 3 or 4 strips. Do not chop - the strips are the texture of this salad.

In a large bowl, stir the mayonnaise (½ cup), Miracle Whip (¼ cup), and wasabi paste (½ tsp) until smooth. Taste, then work in up to another ½ tsp wasabi paste. Dress first, eggs second - wasabi stirred into a bowl of eggs streaks instead of distributing.
Fold the egg strips into the dressing with a spatula, lifting from the bottom rather than stirring, so the strips stay whole. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chill at least 30 minutes before serving. If it sits overnight, taste again before it goes out - wasabi heat is volatile and fades; add another ¼ tsp wasabi paste if it has gone flat.

description: Egg salad with the eggs cut into strips, dressed with mayo, Miracle Whip and a kick of wasabi.

name: Hot Honey Chicken Sandwiches

ingredients.text: ½ bag coleslaw mix (from a 14 oz bag)

instructions.detail: Whisk the mayo (2 Tbsp + 2 tsp), cider vinegar (1 Tbsp), honey (1½ tsp), celery seed (¼ tsp), table salt (⅛ tsp) and black pepper (⅛ tsp). Toss with the coleslaw mix (½ bag) and chill. It holds up to 4 hours because the dressing is vinegar-forward, not heavy mayo.
Pull the meat off the rotisserie chicken (1), discard the skin and bones, and shred it into bite-size pieces. You should have about 3 cups.

In a small saucepan, melt the butter (3 Tbsp) over low heat. Add the garlic (1 clove) for 1 minute, then stir in the honey (¼ cup), hot sauce (2 Tbsp), red pepper flakes (1 tsp), cayenne (½ tsp) and cider vinegar (1½ tsp). Simmer gently 1 to 2 minutes to pull the chili into the fat; a batch this small scorches fast, so watch it. No salt, because the chicken is already seasoned. For milder heat, halve the cayenne.

Melt the butter (1 Tbsp) in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Spread the chicken (3 cups) in a single layer and leave it untouched 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges brown. Three cups usually fits in one batch; split it if the pan is crowded. Rotisserie meat is soft, and these browned edges are the only real texture the filling gets.
Drop the heat to medium-low, pour the hot honey butter over the chicken and toss until glossy and the chicken reads 165°F. Keep the heat low: honey scorches well before the chicken would.
Butter the cut sides of the buns (3) with the butter (1 Tbsp total) and toast them cut-side down in the skillet 1 to 2 minutes. A toasted crumb resists the sauce.
Layer each bottom bun with hot chicken, pickles (½ cup total), slaw and the top bun. Build right before eating so the bun stays crisp.

description: Rotisserie chicken crisped in a hot skillet, tossed in garlicky hot honey butter, and piled on toasted brioche with vinegar slaw and dill pickles.

name: Coconut Rice

ingredients.text: 1⅔ cups coconut milk (one 14 oz can), full-fat or light
2 kaffir lime leaves, crushed in hand

instructions.detail: Rinse the rice (2 cups) until the water runs mostly clear to wash off excess surface starch - it won't go 100% clear. This matters more than for plain rice: coconut milk is thicker than water, so leftover starch turns the rice gluey.
Cover the rinsed rice with water and soak 1 hour, then drain. The head start on water absorption is what lets the grains cook through evenly in the thicker coconut liquid.

Preheat the oven to 400°F. In a saucepan, combine the coconut milk (1⅔ cups), water (1 cup), sugar (5 tsp), and salt (½ tsp) and bring to a boil. Heating the liquid first means the rice starts cooking the moment it hits the oven instead of bloating in lukewarm liquid for 10-15 minutes.

Put the drained rice in a baking pan, tuck in the pandan leaf (1, knotted) or kaffir lime leaves (2, crushed), and pour over the boiling liquid. Cover tightly with foil and bake 40 minutes. The foil traps steam, so this is essentially oven steam-rice with no scorching risk and more even heat than the stovetop.

Pull the pan and rest, still covered in foil, for 15 minutes - don't skip it. The rice finishes cooking and reabsorbs surface moisture, leaving it fluffy. Fluff, discard the leaf, and garnish with toasted desiccated coconut (1 Tbsp) if using.

description: Oven-baked jasmine rice cooked in coconut milk, scented with pandan or kaffir lime leaves.

name: Crispy Onion-and-Black-Pepper Russet Chunks

ingredients.text: 2½ lb russet potatoes (about 3 large), scrubbed, cut into 1-inch chunks
2¼ tsp table salt (for the boiling water)
¼ cup beef tallow, duck fat, or neutral high-heat oil (avocado or refined peanut)
1 large yellow onion, cut into 1-inch wedges, root end intact
3 scallions, green parts only, sliced thin

instructions.detail: Set a rack in the lower third and heat the oven to 450 F with a bare half sheet pan inside holding the tallow (¼ cup). No foil, no parchment - foil is a poor conductor and reflects radiant heat, so potatoes on foil brown noticeably less than on bare aluminum. The pan and fat must be at temperature before the potatoes land; that first contact is where the crust starts.

Cut the russets (2½ lb) into 1-inch chunks, skin on. Keep the variance tight - a pan holding ½-inch and 1½-inch pieces guarantees some burnt and some raw. Skin on gives a second texture; peel them if you want crust on every face.

Bring water (2 qt) to a boil with baking soda (½ tsp) and table salt (2¼ tsp). Add the potatoes and boil 8 to 10 minutes, until a knife tip meets almost no resistance at the edge but the center still holds. Pectin degrades by base-catalyzed beta-elimination, so alkaline water blows out the outer few millimeters far faster than the core. Undershoot and there is no slurry to work with; overshoot and they collapse in the pot.

Drain thoroughly, return to the dry pot, and steam-dry off the heat 1 minute. Add table salt (¾ tsp) and coarse black pepper (1½ tsp), then shake the pot hard for 10 to 15 seconds until the exteriors look fuzzy and pasted over. This is the step people skip. The starch slurry gelatinizes and dehydrates in the oven into a shattering crust - it is the difference between this and ordinary oven fries.

Pull the hot pan, add the potatoes in a single layer with visible gaps between pieces, and return to the 450 F oven. Roast 10 minutes untouched. Crowding parks the surface at 212 F and it will never brown; two pans beat one crowded pan every time.

Drop the oven to 425 F and leave the potatoes alone. Ten minutes at 450 F is all it takes to set the crust; everything after that is driving moisture out of the interiors, and 425 F does that without the set crust going too dark over a 45- to 50-minute roast.

At the 25-minute mark of total roasting time, flip with a thin metal spatula and tuck the onion wedges (1 large) into the gaps. Rotate the pan 180 degrees. Do not flip earlier - an unset crust tears and sticks, while a set crust releases on its own. The rotation covers your oven's hot spot.

Roast 20 to 25 minutes more, until the potatoes are deep brown with crackled edges and the onion is soft and browned at the tips. Total roasting time 45 to 50 minutes. Use convection if you have it; moving air is the right call whenever drying the surface is the goal.

Turn out into a warm bowl, add rice vinegar (1 Tbsp), toss once, then scatter the scallion greens (3) and flaky salt (½ tsp). Serve immediately. Vinegar on the sheet pan would steam the crust; in the bowl it flashes off the hot surfaces and leaves the sharpness behind.

description: Parboiled russet chunks roasted crisp in tallow or duck fat with onion and coarse black pepper, finished with vinegar.

name: Classic Coleslaw Dressing

ingredients.text: Scant ¾ cup mayonnaise (or vegan mayo)
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions.detail: Whisk together the mayo (scant ¾ cup), apple cider vinegar (2 Tbsp), Dijon mustard (1 Tbsp), maple syrup (1 Tbsp), celery seeds (¾ tsp), salt (¼ tsp), garlic powder (1 tsp), onion powder (1 tsp), and black pepper to taste until smooth.
Pour dressing over 6-8 cups coleslaw mix (1 standard store bag). Toss to coat evenly.
Refrigerate for 1-4 hours, stirring occasionally, to let flavors develop.
Keep refrigerated until ready to serve.

description: A creamy coleslaw dressing of mayo, cider vinegar, Dijon and maple syrup with celery seed.

name: Oat Flour Protein Balls

ingredients.text: ½ cup oat flour or almond flour
⅓ cup peanut butter or almond butter
¼ tsp salt (skip if using salted peanut butter)

instructions.detail: Combine the protein powder (¾ cup), oat or almond flour (½ cup), peanut or almond butter (⅓ cup), maple syrup or honey (3 Tbsp), Greek yogurt (1½ Tbsp), and salt (¼ tsp, skip if using salted peanut butter) in a bowl until a dough forms.
Roll into 1-inch balls.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving.

description: No-bake protein balls of vanilla protein powder, oat flour and peanut butter, bound with maple syrup and Greek yogurt.

name: Honey Butter Oat Protein Balls

ingredients.text: 2 Tbsp brown rice syrup or honey
Chocolate chips, nuts, or dried fruit (optional)

instructions.detail: Combine the nut butter (5 Tbsp), brown rice syrup or honey (2 Tbsp), Greek yogurt (2 Tbsp), vanilla protein powder (1½ scoops), melted butter (1 Tbsp), vanilla extract (1 tsp), brown sugar substitute (1 Tbsp), rolled oats (1 cup), and any chocolate chips, nuts, or dried fruit in a bowl until a dough forms.
Roll into balls and refrigerate until firm.

description: No-bake oat protein balls with nut butter, melted butter, honey and Greek yogurt, plus optional chocolate chips or fruit.

name: Peanut Butter Flax Protein Balls

ingredients.text: ¼ cup shredded coconut (optional - note: makes them dry)

instructions.detail: Combine the rolled oats (1½ cups), peanut butter (1 cup), ground flaxseed (¼ cup), honey (¼ cup), protein powder (2 scoops, ¼ cup unflavored), vanilla extract (1 tsp), mini chocolate chips (6 Tbsp), and shredded coconut (¼ cup, optional). If the mixture is too dry, add a splash of water.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Roll into 1-inch balls. Store at room temperature (shelf stable).

description: No-bake balls of rolled oats, peanut butter, flaxseed and honey with protein powder and mini chocolate chips.

name: Cottage Cheese Protein Balls

ingredients.text: 1 cup vanilla or unflavored protein powder
2 Tbsp nut butter (almond, peanut, or cashew)
Dark chocolate chips or cacao nibs

instructions.detail: Blend the cottage cheese (1 cup) until smooth. Combine it with the protein powder (1 cup), nut butter (2 Tbsp), honey or maple syrup (1-2 Tbsp), vanilla extract (1 tsp, optional), and salt (pinch).
Fold in any optional mix-ins.
Roll into balls and refrigerate until firm.

description: High-protein balls made from blended cottage cheese, protein powder and nut butter, with your choice of mix-ins.

name: Almond Butter Greek Yogurt Protein Balls

ingredients.text: A splash of water if needed

instructions.detail: Combine the almond butter (1 cup), Greek yogurt (½ cup), rolled oats (1 cup), ground flax seeds (¼ cup), shredded coconut (⅓ cup), mini chocolate chips (¼ cup), honey or maple syrup (1 Tbsp), and vanilla extract (1 tsp). Roll into 1-inch balls, adding a splash of water if the mixture is too dry.
Refrigerate until firm.

description: No-bake balls of almond butter, Greek yogurt, oats, flax and coconut with mini chocolate chips.

name: Pumpkin Almond Butter Protein Balls

ingredients.text: ¼ cup raw honey (or maple syrup for vegan)

instructions.detail: Combine the rolled oats (1 cup), vanilla protein powder (2 scoops), pumpkin pie spice (1 tsp), almond butter (½ cup), pumpkin puree (⅓ cup), honey or maple syrup (¼ cup), dried cranberries (2 Tbsp), and mini chocolate chips (2 Tbsp). Roll into 1-inch balls.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

description: Pumpkin pie spiced protein balls with oats, almond butter, pumpkin puree, cranberries and chocolate chips.

name: Pumpkin Peanut Butter Protein Balls

ingredients.text: 3 Tbsp pure maple syrup or honey

instructions.detail: Combine the rolled oats (1¼ cups), peanut butter (⅔ cup), vanilla protein powder (½ cup), pumpkin puree (¼ cup), mini chocolate chips (¼ cup), dried cranberries (¼ cup), maple syrup or honey (3 Tbsp), ground flaxseed (1 Tbsp), pumpkin pie spice (2 tsp), and salt (⅛ tsp). Chill the dough for 15 minutes. Roll into 1-inch balls. Refrigerate until firm.

description: Pumpkin pie spiced protein balls with oats, peanut butter, pumpkin puree, flaxseed, cranberries and chocolate chips.

name: Greek Yogurt Brownies

ingredients.text: ½ cup protein powder (chocolate or vanilla)
⅓ cup coconut sugar or granulated sweetener of choice

instructions.detail: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a pan with parchment paper.
Add the Greek yogurt (1 cup), egg (1), cocoa powder (⅓ cup), protein powder (½ cup), and coconut sugar or sweetener (⅓ cup) to a bowl and mix well.
Transfer to baking pan and spread evenly. Optionally top with chocolate chips. Bake for 20-25 minutes until firm and slightly risen.
Let cool completely. Top with flaky sea salt and enjoy.

description: Protein brownies made with Greek yogurt, cocoa powder, protein powder and a single egg.

name: Greek Yogurt Cookie Dough

ingredients.text: ½ cup Greek yogurt (plain or vanilla)
2 Tbsp peanut butter or almond butter
¼ cup oat flour or almond flour

instructions.detail: Mix Greek yogurt (½ cup), peanut butter (2 Tbsp), honey (1 Tbsp), and vanilla (½ tsp) in a bowl until well combined.
Add oat flour (¼ cup) and stir until a dough forms.
Gently fold in chocolate chips (1 Tbsp).
Divide dough into two equal portions. Roll into balls and flatten slightly into a cookie shape.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up.
Enjoy chilled. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

description: Edible cookie dough of Greek yogurt, nut butter, oat flour and chocolate chips.

name: Chicken Noodle Soup

instructions.detail: Simmer whole chicken in broth (6 cups) and water (2 cups) until cooked through. Remove chicken, cool, and shred meat.
Return broth to a boil. Add carrots (3 cups), celery (2 cups), onion (2 cups), and garlic (3 cloves). Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add egg noodles (2 cups), shredded chicken, BBQ sauce (1 Tbsp), and dill weed (2 tsp). Simmer until noodles are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

description: Chicken noodle soup built from a whole chicken with carrots, celery, onion, garlic and egg noodles.

name: Tuscan Chicken Soup

instructions.detail: Simmer the chicken (1 whole) in broth (6 cups) and water (2 cups) until the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F. Remove, cool and shred.
Add onion (1), celery (3 stalks), garlic (3 cloves) and sun-dried tomatoes (½ cup) to the broth. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pasta shells (8 oz) and cook until al dente.
Stir in heavy cream (1 cup) and Parmesan (1 cup). Return the shredded chicken.
Mix cornstarch (2 tsp) with water (2 tsp) and stir in to thicken. Add spinach (2 cups) and cook 2 more minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in white wine vinegar (1 Tbsp). Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

description: Whole-chicken soup with spinach, sun-dried tomatoes and small pasta shells, brightened with white wine vinegar.

name: Chicken Marinade - Sweet Garlic Lime

instructions.detail: Blend the Greek yogurt (½ cup), jalapeño (1, seeds removed), cilantro (⅓ cup), honey (1 Tbsp), lime juice (1 lime), olive oil (1 Tbsp), garlic (1 clove), and salt and pepper together. Coat the chicken (1½ lb) and marinate for at least 1-2 hours before cooking.

description: A blended Greek yogurt marinade for chicken with jalapeño, cilantro, lime, honey and garlic.

name: Chicken Marinade - Spicy Maple Mustard

instructions.detail: Whisk the Dijon mustard (¼ cup), maple syrup (2 Tbsp), olive oil (1 Tbsp), apple cider vinegar (1 Tbsp), garlic powder (1 tsp), paprika (½ tsp), and cayenne (½ tsp) together. Coat the chicken (1½ lb) and marinate for at least 1 hour before cooking.

description: A Dijon and maple syrup chicken marinade with cider vinegar, paprika and cayenne heat.

name: Chicken Marinade - Lemon Herb Yogurt

instructions.detail: Whisk the Greek yogurt (½ cup), lemon juice (2 Tbsp), olive oil (1 Tbsp), garlic (2 cloves), parsley (1 Tbsp), oregano (1 tsp), onion powder (1 tsp), and salt and pepper to taste together. Coat the chicken (1½ lb) and marinate for at least 1 hour before cooking.

description: A Greek yogurt chicken marinade with lemon, garlic, parsley and oregano.

name: Stir-Fry Marinade - Chicken

instructions.detail: Combine the soy sauce (1 Tbsp), water (1 Tbsp), egg white (½), and cornstarch (2 Tbsp). Toss with sliced chicken (1 lb) and marinate for 15-30 minutes before stir-frying (velveting technique).

description: A simple velveting marinade of soy sauce, egg white and cornstarch for tender stir-fried chicken.

name: Strawberry Spinach Smoothie

ingredients.text: 1 cup baby spinach, loosely packed (1 large handful)
1 whole frozen banana, broken into 3 or 4 pieces
1 Tbsp ground flaxseed (must be ground - whole seeds pass through both the blender and the body intact)
½-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced thin (or ¼ tsp ground ginger)
½ cup whole milk, plus more to loosen

instructions.detail: Makes one full 18-oz Magic Bullet cup, about 16 oz of smoothie - one serving. Drop the baby spinach (1 cup, loosely packed) into the cup first; it collapses to almost nothing. Add the frozen strawberries (½ cup), frozen blueberries (¼ cup), and frozen banana (1 whole, broken into 3 or 4 pieces). Skip ice entirely - the banana and the frozen fruit already carry the chill, and ice on top of them overfills the cup and waters the result down.
