Add the Greek yogurt (⅓ cup), peanut butter (1 heaping Tbsp), ground flaxseed (1 Tbsp), and fresh ginger (½-inch piece, peeled and sliced thin, or ¼ tsp ground). Pour the whole milk (½ cup) in LAST. The Magic Bullet cup inverts onto its blade, so whatever goes in last sits against the blade - a blade spinning in liquid throws a vortex that pulls the frozen fruit down into it, while a blade buried in frozen fruit just cavitates and stalls.

Screw on the blade, invert, and run in 15-second bursts, shaking the cup between each one, until smooth - about four bursts. If it stalls, add whole milk 2 Tbsp at a time rather than running the motor longer; the Magic Bullet's motor overheats before it wins an argument with frozen fruit. Never fill past the max line - the seal leaks under pressure.

Spinach carries non-heme iron, which absorbs poorly on its own but noticeably better alongside vitamin C - the strawberries (½ cup) are the biggest vitamin C contributor here, which is why they lead the fruit rather than the blueberries (¼ cup). Peanut butter (1 heaping Tbsp) and ground flaxseed (1 Tbsp) cover magnesium, and the Greek yogurt (⅓ cup) adds the protein that flattens the blood sugar spike a straight fruit smoothie gives you. Ginger (½-inch piece) is the anti-inflammatory note and cuts the flat sweetness of the banana. One tradeoff worth knowing: the calcium in the yogurt and milk does blunt iron absorption somewhat, so treat this as a magnesium-and-protein drink rather than an iron one.

Lower the lactose by swapping the whole milk (½ cup) for lactose-free milk or by cutting it to ¼ cup and loosening with water - the Greek yogurt (⅓ cup) is already strained and low in lactose, so the milk is where most of it sits. Mango (¼ cup frozen) can stand in for the blueberries (¼ cup) but pushes the drink sweeter and drops the vitamin C. Unsweetened cocoa powder (1 Tbsp) adds magnesium and pairs with the peanut butter (1 heaping Tbsp), but fights the berries - use it only if you drop the strawberries (½ cup) and blueberries (¼ cup) and lean on the banana.

description: A spinach, strawberry and blueberry smoothie with banana, Greek yogurt, peanut butter, flax and fresh ginger.

name: Tandoori - Chicken Marinade

instructions.step: Whisk yogurt (1 cup), lemon juice (2 Tbsp), garlic paste (1 Tbsp), ginger paste (1 Tbsp), turmeric (1 tsp), chili powder (1 tsp), cumin (1 tsp), salt (1 tsp), and oil (2 Tbsp).
Rub onto chicken (2 lb) and marinate 4-24 hours.

description: Chicken drumsticks marinated in yogurt, lemon, garlic, ginger, turmeric and Kashmiri chili.

name: Tandoori - Chicken Marinade (Serious Eats)

instructions.step: Mix yogurt (1 cup), lemon juice (2 Tbsp), garlic (from 4 cloves), ginger (1 Tbsp), garam masala (1 tsp), coriander (1 tsp), paprika (1 tsp), cayenne (½ tsp), and salt (1 tsp).
Coat chicken (2 lb) and refrigerate 4-12 hours.

description: Bone-in chicken thighs in a Greek yogurt marinade with garam masala, coriander, paprika and cayenne.

name: Dirty Rice (No-Liver, One Pan)

ingredients.text: 1 can (15.5 oz) kidney beans, drained and rinsed (about 1½ cups)

instructions.detail: Combine the paprika (1 Tbsp), cayenne (1 tsp), black pepper (2 tsp), thyme (1 tsp), oregano (1 tsp), onion powder (1 tsp), garlic powder (1 tsp) and salt (1½ tsp) in a small bowl. Work half of it into the raw ground beef (1 lb) with your hands. Hold the other half back for the vegetables.

Heat a 12-inch skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high, dry. Add the seasoned beef (1 lb), press it flat into one sheet, and leave it alone. 3 to 4 minutes per side, flipping 2 to 3 times, until there is a deep brown crust and browned bits stuck to the pan. Do not stir early and do not pile it up - the surface has to dry before it can brown at all. Water holds the surface at 212F; Maillard browning does not begin until about 266F and does not get good until 285 to 330F. The fond you build here is the entire color and depth budget of this dish.
Pour the rendered fat into a cup, then return about 2 Tbsp to the pan. Break the beef into crumbles. The rice has to toast in fat in step 5, and the seasoning rides into the grain on that fat.

Add the diced onion (1 cup), bell pepper (1 cup) and celery (¾ cup) to the fat over medium. Cook 6 to 8 minutes, until soft and the onion turns translucent heading toward gold. The water they release does the deglazing - scrape as they go and the fond lifts off the pan into the vegetables. Add the minced garlic (4 cloves) and the reserved half of the blend; cook 1 minute, until sharp and fragrant.

Add the rice (1½ cups) dry and stir 2 minutes, until the grains turn chalky-opaque and smell nutty. Fat coating each grain slows water uptake so the grains cook through instead of blowing out - this is what keeps dirty rice from turning to mush.

Add the chicken broth (2¾ cups) and Worcestershire (1 Tbsp), scrape the bottom once more, and bring to a hard boil. Lid on, heat to the lowest setting, 18 minutes. Do not lift the lid. The broth is 2¾ cups rather than a flat 2:1 because the trinity has already put about a third of a cup of its own water in the pan.

Off the heat, scatter the drained and rinsed kidney beans (1 can, 15.5 oz, about 1½ cups) over the surface of the rice without stirring. Lid back on, 10 minutes. They are already cooked and only need to warm through - stirred into the simmer they break down and go pasty, and the loose starch clouds the grain.
Fork the rice through, folding the beans in gently as you go. Fold in the sliced green onions (4) and chopped parsley (¼ cup). Hot sauce goes on the table, not into the pot.

description: One-pan dirty rice made with ground beef instead of chicken livers and seasoned with a Cajun-style spice blend.
